llm.summary: The skill's purpose and instructions are largely coherent, but it instructs installing external plugin code (not bundled), will auto-register and store an API key locally, and exposes commands that reveal that key — you should verify the external package and network behavior before installing.

dimensions.detail: Name and description match the instructions: the skill is a security plugin that registers with a Core API, performs detection via network calls, and stores a local API key. The advertised network domain and local storage path align with the stated purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The SKILL.md instructs the agent/user to install an external plugin package (@openguardrails/moltguard) that is not included in the skill bundle; it also tells the agent to run commands (/og_status, /og_claim) that display the local API key. The skill instructs automatic registration and network calls on first run. Those behaviors are plausible for this purpose but they involve transmitting data and revealing secrets, so they require explicit verification and user consent.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: This is an instruction-only skill that directs installation of an external plugin from a package registry and points to a GitHub repo. Because the plugin code is not bundled, the real security footprint depends entirely on that external package. The install method (registry + GitHub link) is normal, but the installer and code must be audited before trusting network/storage behavior.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required env vars or credentials, which matches the SKILL.md; however it will obtain and locally persist an API key (saved at ~/.openclaw/credentials/moltguard/credentials.json) and provides commands that show that key. Requesting no external secrets is proportional, but automatic creation/storage/display of a secret is a privacy/operational concern that should be considered.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false and the skill does not request system-wide privileges. It will auto-register and persist an API key under its own path, which is expected behavior for a plugin managing its own quota/auth. Autonomous invocation is allowed by default (normal) but combined with network and secret-storage behaviors this increases impact if the external plugin is malicious.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is coherent with its stated purpose but depends on external plugin code you must verify. Before installing: 1) Inspect the referenced GitHub repo and confirm the npm/package registry owner matches the project; 2) Review the code under moltguard/platform-client (or equivalent) to confirm only hashes — not raw content or secrets — are sent; 3) Verify the TLS ownership of api.openguardrails.com and the exact API endpoints used; 4) Run the install in a sandbox or disposable environment first; 5) Be cautious with /og_status and /og_claim as they reveal the API key — avoid running them in shared terminals or logging outputs; 6) Consider creating a dedicated (limited) account or API key for testing and monitor network traffic during onboarding. If you cannot audit the external package, treat installation as higher risk.
